chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Husayn ibn Saif, from Abu Jameela, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the servant frequents in seeking the Forgiveness, his parchment (record of deeds) is raised and it would be gleaming'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual effect of frequent istighfar on a believer's record of deeds?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the transformative power of istighfar, describing how consistent repentance causes the believer's scroll of deeds to be elevated and radiate light, symbolizing spiritual purity and divine acceptance. This imagery reflects the Shia understanding of istighfar not merely as a verbal act but as a means of cleansing the soul, ensuring that one's record stands out brightly among the records of others on the Day of Resurrection. The 'gleaming' of the sheet serves as a metaphor for the clarity and weight of good deeds that result from sincere repentance.
